transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net advanced technical support, my name is Darren. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Darren. I am having a massive headache with your Hub Pro router. My wireless HP LaserJet printer is connected to the two-point-four gigahertz band, but none of my laptops on the five gigahertz band can discover it via mDNS or AirPrint!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can help with local network configuration. Let's start with security verification. What is your full name and billing address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Faisal Qureshi, 102 Highfield Lane, Southampton, SO17 1RN.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the four-digit security PIN on the account, Faisal?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What IP address has the Hub Pro DHCP server assigned to that HP printer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It has a static DHCP reservation at 192.168.1.140.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you ping 192.168.1.140 from a laptop on the five gigahertz network?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, standard ICMP ping replies in two milliseconds, so Layer 3 IP routing works, but UDP port 5353 multicast packets are being blocked completely by the router!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub Pro firmware enabled Wireless Client Isolation by default in the recent security patch.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why on earth would you turn on client isolation by default on a home router? It breaks every wireless printer and Chromecast in the house! I've wasted my entire evening trying to print tax documents!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Client isolation prevents untrusted IoT devices from probing other computers on the local subnet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I know what it does, but there should have been a clear toggle or warning in the firmware release notes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously users who want cross-band multicast discovery can disable the isolation toggle in the web admin GUI.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Where is the toggle? I looked under Advanced Wireless and couldn't see it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open your web browser and navigate to 192.168.1.1.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Logged into the Hub Pro admin console now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on the 'Advanced' tab on the left navigation bar.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicked Advanced.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now click on 'LAN IP & Subnets', then scroll down to 'Multicast & mDNS Filtering'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I see 'IGMP Snooping' and 'Wireless Client Isolation'. Both have green checkmarks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are you using band steering where both frequencies share the same SSID name, or separate network names?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Both frequencies share the single SSID name 'HomeNetwork'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And does the printer have a strong Wi-Fi signal rating in the web GUI device table?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It shows negative sixty-two dBm, which is about four out of five bars.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is an ideal signal level for a stationary printer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it has a direct line of sight through the open doorway to the router.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you don't have any third-party Wi-Fi mesh extenders in between the router and printer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, just the standalone Hub Pro router in the study.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Uncheck the box that says 'Wireless Client Isolation'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unchecked.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And make sure the box for 'IGMP Snooping' remains checked, because that enables efficient multicast packet forwarding between bands.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: IGMP Snooping is checked. Clicking Apply Changes now. This whole setup has been an utter nightmare!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The wireless chipsets will take about thirty seconds to reload the bridging tables. Bear with me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Faisal. Now what is the IP address of that HP printer on your network again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Like I said earlier, it's 192.168.1.140.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, open the print dialogue on your laptop on the five gigahertz Wi-Fi now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening System Settings on my MacBook... Printers & Scanners... Clicking Add Printer...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the HP LaserJet show up under the Bonjour discovery list?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! 'HP LaserJet Pro M404dw [Bonjour]' appeared instantly! Selecting it now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Send a test page to confirm bidirectional communication.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Printing test page... The printer in the other room just whirred into life and printed the test sheet!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you also check if your phone can see it via AirPrint over Wi-Fi?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opened a PDF on my iPhone, tapped share, tapped Print... Yes, the printer shows up with ink levels displayed!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms mDNS discovery is operating cleanly across both the two-point-four and five gigahertz bands.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That was the exact setting I needed. Thank you Darren.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm your account contact telephone number, it is 07700 900481, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my mobile.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm for the record, the installation address is 102 Highfield Lane, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 102 Highfield Lane.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will leave the notes on this ticket so any future firmware updates do not re-enable client isolation on your profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I really appreciate that, I don't want to go through this again after the next update.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your Hub Pro settings I can assist you with today, Faisal?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, everything else is configured exactly how I want it. Thanks for the quick fix.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Faisal, and have a great rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Darren, you too. Goodbye.
